Release them to physicians only, since role-based access satisfies Part 2
why: Part 2 records need consent specific to that category, and a general treatment opt-in is not sufficient for a routine query. Removing names does not make a clinical query meaningful or satisfy the rule. Role-based access limits who can look but is not a substitute for patient consent. A genuine medical emergency has separate, documented handling.

q: A message can pass every structural validation check and still be a data-quality failure.
opts: True
False
why: Validation checks form, such as types and lengths. A mapping that places a value into the wrong code system, or a feed that arrives hours late, still passes those checks while degrading accuracy or timeliness. That is why mapping review and monitoring go beyond schema validation.

q: Which disclosure is generally exempt from HIPAA's minimum necessary standard?
opts: Giving a billing vendor the full chart to process one claim
Giving a researcher every field when only medication data is needed
Sending a patient's records to a specialist who is treating that patient
Giving a quality analyst all fields for an internal improvement review
why: Disclosures to a provider for treatment are exempt, so a specialist can receive what is clinically relevant without trimming. Payment, research, and healthcare operations disclosures are all subject to minimum necessary, which is why a full chart for one claim or an over-broad research extract is a problem even when the recipient is legitimate.

q: A vendor that will host PHI for an integration project has signed an SLA and a strong NDA and says nothing more is needed. What is still missing?
opts: A cap on uptime penalties for any outage that lasts more than a day
A statement of which FHIR version the vendor will use for the interface
A statistician's certification that the data is de-identified for the vendor
A BAA covering permitted uses, safeguards, and breach-reporting duties for PHI
why: HIPAA requires a business associate agreement before a vendor handles PHI, and it covers permitted uses, safeguards, and breach reporting, which an SLA and an NDA do not. Penalty caps and FHIR versions are commercial and technical terms. A de-identification certification would apply only if the data were not PHI at all.

q: How does TEFCA differ from a regional HIE?
opts: TEFCA lets networks exchange under common terms; an HIE links participants within one network
TEFCA replaces HIPAA's privacy rules for any exchange that crosses between networks
TEFCA is a single national database holding every patient's records
A regional HIE is limited to one EHR vendor, while TEFCA is vendor-neutral
why: An HIE is a network of participants, while TEFCA is a framework of common legal and technical terms intended to let those networks exchange with each other without bilateral deals. HIPAA still applies. TEFCA does not store records centrally, and regional HIEs are generally vendor-neutral, so the vendor distinction is backwards.

q: A hospital wants a nurse's access to depend on her role and also on whether she is assigned to the patient's unit during her shift. Which model fits?
opts: Break-the-glass, which grants access whenever a user supplies a reason
Discretionary access, where each record's owner grants access by hand
Role-based control alone, since the role already carries every context a decision needs
Attribute-based control, which evaluates context such as unit assignment alongside the role
why: Attribute-based control combines role with attributes of the user, resource, and situation, such as assignment and shift. Break-the-glass is an audited exception, not a routine model. Discretionary access does not scale in a hospital. A role alone cannot express whether this nurse is assigned to this patient right now.

q: If a user states a reason when breaking the glass, the access is considered justified and no after-the-fact review is needed.
opts: True
False
why: The stated reason is the start of accountability, not the end. Break-the-glass access is flagged for mandatory review so a privacy or compliance team can confirm the access was truly needed. Without review it would be an unmonitored back door.

q: Which controls are appropriate for emergency access to a record? (Choose three.)
opts: Requiring the user to state a reason at the time of access
Sending each override to a privacy team for after-the-fact review
Granting the user a permanent role upgrade after the first override
Time-limiting the elevated access
Pausing audit logging during emergencies to avoid delay
why: A stated reason, review, and a time limit keep an exception accountable and temporary. A permanent role upgrade turns an exception into standing access, and turning off logging removes the very evidence that makes emergency access defensible.

q: An EMPI links records whose addresses differ by comparing them with a large third-party reference database of people's historical demographics. Which approach is this?
opts: Deterministic matching on a single exact field such as the MRN
Referential matching, which resolves identity against an outside reference set
Probabilistic matching on weighted field agreement between the records alone
Content-based routing on the facility values found inside each message
why: Referential matching uses an outside data set of known identities to resolve records whose demographics changed or were entered differently. Deterministic matching needs exact agreement on specific fields, and probabilistic matching weighs agreement among the records themselves without an external reference. Content-based routing is an integration-engine technique unrelated to identity.

q: A data steward can reject an interface mapping change that violates the agreed definition of a data domain even though the engine would run it without error.
opts: True
False
why: Stewardship is about owning the definition and quality rules of the data, independent of whether a mapping is technically valid. A translation that the engine happily executes can still change a coded value's meaning, and the steward is the person accountable for catching that.

q: Two hospital systems are combining their MPIs. Which steps are sound? (Choose three.)
opts: Run matching across both populations with a review queue for borderline scores
Assign an enterprise identifier that cross-references facility MRNs without overwriting them
Auto-merge every pair with the same name and date of birth to finish quickly
Pilot on a sample and measure false matches before linking in bulk
Delete the smaller system's MPI before matching begins, to avoid duplicate work
why: Review queues, cross-referencing identifiers while preserving source MRNs, and measuring error rates on a pilot are sound practices. Name and birth date alone also match different people, so blind auto-merging creates overlays. Deleting an MPI before matching destroys the identity history that matching depends on.
